Hi Alice — great meeting. High-level answers inline and attaching a one-pager + SOW draft.

1) Packaging summary (short):
- Optimize as an add-on: billed monthly as a feature bundle when on Dedicated or Hosted (recommended for customers using Dedicated GPU pools).
- Committed Optimize Credits: pre-paid credits that reduce per-token billing for inference when Optimize suggestions are applied (batching/caching/quantization).
- Managed Reserved Bundle: fixed monthly fee that includes Optimize + dedicated support + X optimization hours.

2) Economics of batching/caching:
- Batching reduces per-token CPU/GPU scheduling overhead — visible as a token cost reduction in the usage report (we meter post-optimization token-equivalent).
- Prefix/KV caching reduces repeated compute for common context windows — can drop effective token counts on retried/partial prompts.
- Quantization recommendations affect model variants (e.g., int8 vs fp16); switching to a quantized variant lowers raw compute cost; Optimize applies a safety margin so quality regressions are kept below a customer-defined threshold.

Discounts/intro credits: we typically offer a 3-month trial credit for Optimize ($10k) + an onboarding credit for model tuning for first-year committed customers. For a 12-month committed credit (>$200k commit) we can offer a bundled 15% credit + one month free of the reserved bundle. Exact discounting is negotiation-dependent — Karthik/Marissa, can you confirm floor here?

Attachments: Redwood_Optimize_Pricing_v1.pdf, SOW_CloudBridge_v3.docx

Cheers,
Sooj
